newsitem.title: UK: Soft oils threaten palm oil's dominance of market.
newsitem.headline: Soft oils threaten palm oil's dominance of market.

text.p: High palm oil prices in Malaysia are threatening its share of the market, European vegetable oil traders said.
"People are getting fed up with palm oil because it is so overpriced and no one can understand why because demand is not there," said one trader.

One of Malaysia's major palm oil buyers, India, has recently started to replace some of it's palm olein offtake with sunflower oil with a purchase of 100,000 tonnes for delivery during January and February.
"It's hardly surprising that India is buying sunoil when you think that it is at a $80 to $90 discount against olein," said a trader.
Traders said sunflower oil is at such a big discount to palm olein that it can be shipped from Europe to any part of the Far East at a profit.
"Sunoil is very cheap at the moment not only against palm oil but also against soy oil where there is a $30 to $35 a tonne discount," said another trader.
However, traders said prices were not the only consideration.
"At one time people just bought on price, but now if they decide they want brand X they will buy it regardless," one said.
Recently China has been buying rape oil, not because of price, but because it's is popular as a cooking oil in the south of the country.
Traders said the market was quiet at the moment owing to holidays in different parts of the world, but the next seven to ten days could set the trend for the coming three to four mouths.
"We've got the USDA report on Wednesday, which people will be watching." one said.

If the USDA report shows a soybean carry out figure of around 140 to 145 million bushels as at September 1, then that would be within expectations, however any figure above or below that will move the market, traders said.

The other major factor in the soft oils market is the south American crop...."which is being upgraded all the time,' said one trader. At the moment the Argentine soybean crop is estimated at around 14 million tonnes while Brazil's crop is projected at 27 million tonnes, traders said.
As ever, the market is looking for demand with China the main focus of its attention.
"People want to see not only how much vegetable oil China buys, but what kind and from where," said a trader.
